name: Stanisław Trembecki
credit: Portrait of Stanisław Trembecki by Johann Baptist von Lampi the Elder (18th century) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Stanisław Trembecki (1739–1812) was a Polish poet and translator of the Enlightenment. He belonged to the circle of King Stanisław August Poniatowski and wrote occasional verse, fables, epigrams and political lyrics, among them "Na dzień siódmy września" and "Nadgrobek hajduka".

In his later years he lived at the court of the magnate Szczęsny Potocki at Tulczyn in Ukraine. There he wrote his descriptive poem "Zofijówka" in praise of the park Potocki laid out at Uman and named for his wife Zofia.
